coverage.reason: States the extended parallel run and mandatory route from 30 November 2024.
Identifies launch, portal, submission categories and an earlier circular whose contents are unavailable.
Establishes acceptance of existing channels during the original parallel run.
Heading introducing the extension and enhancements.
Explains monitoring and consultation; supplies no selected routing condition.
Confirms extension through 29 November 2024; enhancements explain its purpose.
Restates mandatory routing, identifies integration examples and separately permits annual-fee payment.
Operational review and contact guidance do not qualify the mandatory route.
Supplies the investment-product categories attached to IPD scope.
Expands WINGS; adds no routing duty.

dimensions.explanation: The duty concerns persons making covered applications or submissions to IPD, without specifying their institutional role. Product administration and the footnote constrain scope; this is not a general duty for every industry participant.
The footnote lists relevant product categories, and WINGS is expanded. The boundaries of 'applications and submissions', including fee-only transactions, are not exhaustively defined.

Existing channels remain available during the parallel run on the natural reading of its extension. No post-cutover exemption is stated. 'Where practicable' qualifies SFC review and enhancement, not mandatory submission.
'Must' imposes routing; 'will be integrated' announces system migration; 'can also' permits annual-fee payment through e-IP without expressly requiring it.

Launch was 29 July 2024; the original 29 October endpoint is extended to 29 November; mandatory routing begins inclusively on 30 November 2024. Treatment of submissions in pending cases is not expressly addressed.

The earlier circular dated 8 July 2024 is referenced but not supplied. Dependency missing.4ad6b317ad4ade41b82f120a is unresolved and cannot confidently be identified with that circular. Additional operational or transitional provisions cannot be inferred.

questions: What text does dependency missing.4ad6b317ad4ade41b82f120a supply, and is it the circular dated 8 July 2024?
Do further submissions after cutover in cases opened through existing channels require migration, and what event determines the submission date?
Does the product footnote exhaust IPD scope, and how are borderline transactions classified?
Are fee-only transactions separately subject to a mandatory payment-channel rule elsewhere?

assumptions: The selected control is the route used for one actual application or submission, not overall regulatory compliance.
The submission event date governs cutover even when the underlying case began earlier; the packet states no grandfathering rule.
Extending the parallel run carries forward acceptance of existing channels through 29 November 2024.
Annual-fee payment alone is not classified as a mandatory submission merely because e-IP supports it.
No exception from unavailable material is assumed.

citations.quote: After the extended period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by the Investment Products Division (IPD)1 must be submitted to IPD via e-IP from 30 November 2024.
During this period, the SFC continues to accept applications and submissions via existing channels.
To facilitate these enhancements, the SFC will extend the parallel run period of e-IP by one month to 29 November 2024.
The current submission requests from IPD via the IP E-submission system will be integrated into e-IP, including reporting of net asset values, large redemptions and suspensions of dealing.
In addition, e-IP users can also settle recurring annual fees associated with relevant investment products through the new system.

1 Investment-linked assurance schemes, mandatory provident fund products, open-ended fund companies, paper gold schemes, pooled retirement funds, real estate investment trusts, unit trusts and mutual funds and unlisted structured investment products.

readings.distinction: Submission-event routing is the strongest supported reading: the text covers applications and submissions without limiting the mandate to newly opened cases. A new-cases-only alternative would materially spare later filings in existing cases, but the supplied text does not support that exception sufficiently to formalize it as a competing reading. The strongest uncertainty is transitional treatment in unavailable referenced material.
